_meta.source: Traditional reference entries drawn from commonly-cited Navagraha Jadi (root-remedy) folk-astrology practice; verify each entry against an authoritative source before treating as final.
_meta.verification: Expanded to 9 of 9 graha keys used by the application. Several mappings remain low-confidence folk traditions and are explicitly labelled as such rather than presented as medically validated prescriptions.

jadis.purpose: Traditionally worn to support solar (Sun) strength — vitality, authority, father/government-related matters.
jadis.traditionalUsage: Root is cleaned, tied in red thread, and worn as an armband/pendant, or kept in the puja area.
jadis.wearingMethod: Worn on Sunday morning after ritual purification, ideally on the right upper arm.
jadis.precautions: Traditional folk remedy only — not a medical treatment; discontinue if any skin irritation occurs; consult a qualified practitioner before use.
jadis.confidence: Low-Moderate — folk-astrology attribution, regional variation exists
jadis.source: Sample entry — commonly-cited Navagraha Jadi practice

jadis.purpose: Traditionally used to support Moon (mind, emotional steadiness, mother-related matters).
jadis.traditionalUsage: Root worn as a pendant or kept under the pillow; also used in classical Ayurveda as a nervine herb (distinct claim from the astrological one).
jadis.wearingMethod: Worn or placed on Monday, ideally during the waxing lunar fortnight (Shukla Paksha).
jadis.precautions: Traditional folk remedy only — not a medical treatment; the Ayurvedic herbal use of Brahmi is a separate, evidence-different claim and should not be conflated with the astrological practice.
jadis.confidence: Low-Moderate — folk-astrology attribution, regional variation exists
jadis.source: Sample entry — commonly-cited Navagraha Jadi practice

jadis.wearingMethod: Worn on Tuesday morning after ritual purification.

jadis.confidence: Low-Moderate — folk-astrology attribution, regional variation exists
